free_tier.stated: When you create a new AWS Free Tier account, you get $100 in credits immediately. As you explore key services, you can earn up to $100 more. That's up to $200 over 6 months ... The account closes on its own 6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first.

egress.terms: $100 of credit at $0.09 per GB is 1.01 TiB, or $200 for 2.02 TiB, plus 100 GB a month free; across 6 months that is 0.26 to 0.43 TiB a month; ingress: udp
egress.free_allowance: $100 of credit at $0.09 per GB is 1.01 TiB, or $200 for 2.02 TiB, plus 100 GB a month free; across 6 months that is 0.26 to 0.43 TiB a month

interface_detail: AWS CLI and the EC2 API
tooling: wg-quick on the instance; AWS CLI for the security group and Elastic IP
chaining: one EC2 instance for up to 6 months on the credit, with the 100 GB a month free egress as the only recurring free volume

limits.value: $100 to $200 of egress at $0.09 per GB is 1.01 to 2.02 TiB, plus 100 GB a month free
the account closes 6 months after it opens or when the credits run out, whichever comes first

binding_note: at 1 TiB a month the $100 of guaranteed credit is spent in about 35 days, and the 100 GB a month free egress covers only a tenth of one month. The 6-month clock is not what stops it; the money is.

identity_cost.detail: a credit or debit card at signup for identity verification; the page says 'You won't be charged unless you convert to a Paid plan'

reliability_note: the account and every resource in it are closed at 6 months without conversion to a paid plan
confidence_note: the rate comes from the machine-readable price feed the EC2 pricing page renders, at us-east-1; a probe would confirm the same rate is charged against a trial's credits, which needs an account

evidence.proved: 'you get $100 in credits immediately ... you can earn up to $100 more. That's up to $200 over 6 months' and 'The account closes on its own 6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first'
'AWS customers receive 100 GB of free data transfer out to the internet free each month, aggregated across all AWS Services and Regions (except China and GovCloud)'
the price feed the EC2 page renders: us-east-1 'DataTransfer External Outbound Next 10 TB' price 0.0900000000 and 'DataTransfer External Inbound' price 0.0000000000, published 2026-09-16

notes: Arithmetic: $100 over $0.09 a GB is 1,111 GB = 1.01 TiB, and $200 is 2,222 GB = 2.02 TiB. Spread across the 6 months the account lives, $100 is $16.67 a month, or 185 GB, plus the 100 GB free each month, so 285 GB = 0.28 TiB a month; with the full $200 it is 0.43 TiB. The old 12-month Free Tier with 100 GB a month egress for a year is gone from this page; what replaced it is a credit that a reader has to earn half of. The always-free line, which the page describes as '30+ AWS services are always free within monthly usage limits', does not include a t3.micro with a public IPv4.

extras.wg_detail: an EC2 instance with an Elastic IP or a public IPv4; wg-quick binds UDP natively
extras.volume_stated: $100 of credit at $0.09 per GB is 1.01 TiB, or $200 for 2.02 TiB, plus 100 GB a month free; across 6 months that is 0.26 to 0.43 TiB a month
